confidence_notes: I based the food anchors on aggregated cost-of-living sites for El Nido (traveltables, combien-coute, citycost, and similar) from one web search. Those sites gave about USD 5 for an inexpensive meal, about USD 29.5 for a three-course meal for two, USD 2.1 to 3.75 for a cappuccino, and about USD 1.2 to 2.6 for a San Miguel in a restaurant or bar. The sources disagree, and El Nido's tourist pricing is above the Philippine average, so I set the anchors toward the middle-to-upper part of those ranges. My search did not return dedicated aggregated prices for cocktails or wine. I estimated them from the local price relationship to beer and from typical prices in Philippine resort towns, so they are less certain. In El Nido, most wine is imported and has a markup. The accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge. I did not check live listings. El Nido accommodation is expensive for Southeast Asia, and July is the wet low season, so rates may be somewhat below peak-season levels. The FX value is the RBA's 4pm AUD/USD rate for 18 November 2026, as reported by search results that point to RBA pages. I did not open the RBA page itself.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared El Nido with Philippine island tourist hubs such as Coron and Boracay, which have tourist premiums on food and drinks above Manila and provincial prices. As a regional check, it is broadly similar to Southeast Asian beach destinations such as Koh Phi Phi.
